articles.summary: Bank of America will host more than 500 technology companies and investors for its 15th annual Technology Innovation Summit in San Francisco on October 7. The summit brings founders and venture capital firms together with Bank of America leaders from Global Technology, Technology Investment Banking and Capital Markets to examine how emerging technology is changing banking and the wider economy.

articles.summary: Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), Blackstone (NYSE: BX), Citi (NYSE: C) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) (the “Lead Financial Partners”) today announced a $63 billion transaction to enable the deployment of AI compute capacity, leveraging Broadcom Inc.’s (NASDAQ: AVGO) technology, for Anthropic. This transaction is part of the strategic compute capacity agreement previously announced by Broadcom, with an expected delivery starting in calendar 2027.
articles.title: Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley Announce Landmark sixty three billion dollars $63 Billion Financing Structure to Enable AI Compute Capacity in Partnership with Broadcom

articles.summary: Black Friday traditionally marks the unofficial start of the holiday shopping season, however this year consumers are planning to make their biggest holiday shopping push a little later. According to the Bank of America 2026 Holiday Spending Survey, 29% of consumers plan to do most of their holiday shopping in early to mid-December, up from 19% in 2025. Meanwhile, those planning to concentrate most of their shopping around Black Friday fell from 25% to 17%.
articles.title: Bank of America Study: Early December Could Overtake Black Friday as the Peak Holiday Shopping Window This Year

articles.summary: Bank of America today announced its Personal Retirement Strategy (PRS) program has surpassed $100 billion in total assets, including more than $10 billion in assets under management by Merrill Managed.
articles.title: Bank of America Personal Retirement Strategy Surpasses 100 billion dollars $100 Billion as Demand for Personalized Retirement Solutions Accelerates

articles.summary: Bank of America continues to expand and modernize its financial center network, reflecting the important role in-person expertise plays when serving clients, alongside the growing use of digital banking. Wisconsin is the latest state added to the national network, with the company opening its first financial centers in Madison and Milwaukee this month. Bank of America plans to open 19 financial centers across the state through 2030. In Q1 2027, the bank will open centers in Birmingham, Alabama, and in Greater New Orleans later in the year.
articles.title: Bank of America Opens First Financial Centers in Wisconsin, Sets 2027 Entry into Alabama and Louisiana

articles.summary: Bank of America announced it has been named to PEOPLE’s 2026 100 Companies That Care list. This marks the bank’s eighth consecutive year on the list, underscoring its long-standing commitment to supporting teammates and local communities. To create the list, PEOPLE partnered with Great Place to Work® to analyze confidential feedback from nearly 970,000 employees at major U.S. employers, alongside data on workplace benefits, corporate culture and community giving.
articles.title: Bank of America Named to PEOPLE’s 100 Companies That Care List for Eighth Consecutive Year

Each will sell to holiday shoppers for more than two weeks, and the bank will cover rent and booth build-out.

articles.title: Bank of America in Partnership with Fundación También Brings new Youth Sports Initiative to Spain

articles.summary: The Bank of America Chicago Marathon celebrated its 48th running Sunday as more than 54,000 participants made their way through 29 Chicago neighborhoods. Amos Kipruto (KEN) battled to the front in the men’s competition, breaking the tape in the second fastest time ever on U.S. soil, 2:01:09, while Hawi Feysa (ETH) defended her title, capturing the women’s crown in 2:13:33, making her the fourth fastest woman in history. Emma Grace Hurley (USA) dazzled in her first marathon, breaking the American debut record with a 2:20:47 while Clayton Young (USA) became the second fastest American man ever, running 2:05:23.
articles.title: Champions Rise and Make History at the 48th Bank of America Chicago Marathon
